clauses.reason: Exhausted by performance on August 18, 1959, the date the order was signed. Its only operative words revoke Executive Order No. 9887 of August 22, 1947, which designated the Preparatory Commission for the International Refugee Organization and its successor as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act, a one-time act that commands nothing afterwards. The order has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed; the Federal Register issue of August 20, 1959 is the alternative reading and is disclosed here. Actor: the order itself; the end source is its own operative text. The revoked order's non-operation is the surviving consequence, not a continuing command.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10832 (24 FR 6753, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of August 20, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10832.txt), headed Executive Order 10832, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on August 18, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Revocation of EO 9887, Designating Certain  Public International Organizations Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges,  Exemptions, and Immunities). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order has one operative sentence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 9887 of August 22, 1947, which designated the Preparatory Commission for the International Refugee Organization and its successor as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. The order also has two recitals, one stating what Executive Order 9887 did and one stating that those organizations have ceased to exist, and an enacting clause citing section 1 of the International Organizations Immunities Act; neither recital is a separate command. The order states no effective date, so it took effect when signed on August 18, 1959; the Federal Register printed it on August 20, 1959, which is the alternative date a reader might take for effectiveness. The revocation is a single act that the order performs by its own words when it issues; once made it commands nothing further, so the clause is exhausted by performance on the signing date. What survives is the fact that the revoked order no longer operates, which is a consequence of the act and not a continuing command of this order. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
